patients.label: Case 1: 45-year-old woman with stage IV ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma, alectinib liver toxicity and hemolytic anemia, switched to brigatinib

identity_evidence.quote: A 45-year-old Caucasian female, smoker, presented initially for dyspnea and chest pain in March 2020.

attribution_limitations: The text gives platelets 'normal ... in the range of 250–300 × 10^(9)/L' while Table 2 gives 306 for the diagnosis of hemolytic anemia; the text range and the table value are not stated to be the same time point and are kept as separate facts.
Alectinib is reported as stopped as of late August 2020 and brigatinib as initiated in October 2020 after a 4-week recovery period; no exact dates are given.

patients.label: Case 2: 80-year-old woman with stage IV ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma, severe aortic stenosis and recurrent alectinib-induced hemolytic anemia, switched to brigatinib

identity_evidence.quote: An 80-year-old middle eastern female, smoker, with multiple comorbidities

attribution_limitations: Patient 2 has three overlapping laboratory descriptions that do not agree: the text (early November 2019: MCV 83 fL, reticulocytes 143, haptoglobin <0.3 g/L, indirect bilirubin up to 25), the Table 1 row labelled 2019–10 (late) (MCV 83, platelets 181, total bilirubin 21, haptoglobin 1.57, reticulocytes 124) and Table 2 'upon diagnosis' (MCV 84, platelets 234, indirect/total bilirubin 25 (52), haptoglobin <0.3, reticulocytes 142). The source does not state that these are one time point, so each is kept as its own timed fact and none is merged or declared the correct value.
The text places the hospitalization with Hb 67 g/L in early November 2019, whereas Table 1 labels the Hb 67 g/L row 2019–10 (late); the 2019–11 row shows Hb 80 g/L.
The text says Brigatinib was initiated as of August 2020, while the Table 1 row labelled 2020–09 reads 'Replaced by Brigatinib'; the table does not state a start date.

The text says Hb rose to 133 g/L on follow-up testing after alectinib was stopped in early April 2020, whereas the Table 1 April row shows Hb 128 g/L and the June row Hb 133 g/L; the text also states Hb 133 g/L after brigatinib start, matching the September row.
Table 1 shows 450 mg BID in the 2020–07 row, but the text gives no dose for the late-June 2020 rechallenge and describes permanent discontinuation in July 2020.

The discussion states that all patients had normal iron, vitamin B12 and folate, but Patient 2's case text reports serum iron 6.6 µmol/L and iron/transferrin saturation 11% without calling them normal, and never mentions B12 or folate. B12 and folate normal are copied from the explicit 'All patients' sentence; the iron-normal statement is also copied but kept review_only.
The Table 1 footnote says red script marks abnormal values, but no colour survives in the retained text, so no high/low flag is assigned to table cells.

Figure 2B is captioned as variation of the brain lesion within less than one month on treatment; the month-year labels printed under the two images are treated as exam dates and not transcribed, and the caption interval is recorded as stated.

The discussion says that in all 4 patients the RBC membrane was altered with acanthocytes, echinocytes and spherocytes, whereas Patient 2's own smear lists anisocytosis, acanthocytes and echinocytes without spherocytes. The discussion sentence is not copied as a separate smear result.

attribution_limitations: Patient 2 has three overlapping laboratory descriptions that do not agree: the text (early November 2019: MCV 83 fL, reticulocytes 143, haptoglobin <0.3 g/L, indirect bilirubin up to 25), the Table 1 row labelled 2019–10 (late) (MCV 83, platelets 181, total bilirubin 21, haptoglobin 1.57, reticulocytes 124) and Table 2 'upon diagnosis' (MCV 84, platelets 234, indirect/total bilirubin 25 (52), haptoglobin <0.3, reticulocytes 142). The source does not state that these are one time point, so each is kept as its own timed fact and none is merged or declared the correct value.
The text places the hospitalization with Hb 67 g/L in early November 2019, whereas Table 1 labels the Hb 67 g/L row 2019–10 (late); the 2019–11 row shows Hb 80 g/L.
The text says Brigatinib was initiated as of August 2020, while the Table 1 row labelled 2020–09 reads 'Replaced by Brigatinib'; the table does not state a start date.

The text says Hb rose to 133 g/L on follow-up testing after alectinib was stopped in early April 2020, whereas the Table 1 April row shows Hb 128 g/L and the June row Hb 133 g/L; the text also states Hb 133 g/L after brigatinib start, matching the September row.
Table 1 shows 450 mg BID in the 2020–07 row, but the text gives no dose for the late-June 2020 rechallenge and describes permanent discontinuation in July 2020.

The discussion states that all patients had normal iron, vitamin B12 and folate, but Patient 2's case text reports serum iron 6.6 µmol/L and iron/transferrin saturation 11% without calling them normal, and never mentions B12 or folate. B12 and folate normal are copied from the explicit 'All patients' sentence; the iron-normal statement is also copied but kept review_only.
The Table 1 footnote says red script marks abnormal values, but no colour survives in the retained text, so no high/low flag is assigned to table cells.

Figure 2B is captioned as variation of the brain lesion within less than one month on treatment; the month-year labels printed under the two images are treated as exam dates and not transcribed, and the caption interval is recorded as stated.

The discussion says that in all 4 patients the RBC membrane was altered with acanthocytes, echinocytes and spherocytes, whereas Patient 2's own smear lists anisocytosis, acanthocytes and echinocytes without spherocytes. The discussion sentence is not copied as a separate smear result.
